mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 330e engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a BMW 330e costs £1,200-£6,500 depending on condition and generation. Used B48 engines start from £1,200, reconditioned units range from £2,500-£5,000, and fully rebuilt engines with warranty cost £3,500-£6,500. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 due to the hybrid system complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a BMW 330e?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include coolant loss without visible leaks, oil filter housing leaks (oil or coolant on the driveway), VANOS-related hesitation on acceleration, cold-start rattle (timing chain tensioner), and drivetrain fault codes (often caused by a weak 12V battery).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 330e?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the generation and condition of the car. A typical 330e is worth £18,000-£45,000 depending on age and mileage. A rebuilt engine at £3,500-£6,500 is well within the vehicle's value for modern G20 examples. For older F30 examples (2016-2019), assess the car's overall condition and battery health before committing.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 330e engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement takes 3-5 days for a specialist due to the hybrid system complexity - including removal of the old unit, HV system isolation, fitting the replacement, and testing. Some suppliers offer delivery on used engines, but fitting always requires workshop time.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B48B20M0, B48B20M1 and B48B20O1 engines in the 330e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B48B20M0 (2016-2019) produces 252 hp combined and was fitted to the F30 330e. The B48B20M1 (2019-2020) introduced XtraBoost, taking total output to 292 hp. The B48B20O1 (2020-present) maintains 292 hp but features revised engine management and a larger 12kWh battery for improved electric range.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW 330e engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind. Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 330e - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 330e debuted in 2016 as the first plug-in hybrid variant of the 3 Series, part of BMW's iPerformance electrification strategy. Over two generations - the F30 (2016-2019) and G20 (2019-present) - the 330e has combined BMW's acclaimed B48 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine with an electric motor integrated into the ZF 8-speed automatic transmission. Total system power has grown from 252 hp to 292 hp, with electric-only range increasing from 22 miles to over 40 miles.

milestones.description: B48B20M0, 2.0L turbocharged four-cylinder petrol with 80kW electric motor, 252 hp combined (F30 330e iPerformance)
B48B20M1, 2.0L turbocharged four-cylinder petrol, XtraBoost function (41 hp extra for 10 seconds), 292 hp combined (G20 330e)
B48B20O1, revised engine variant with larger 12kWh battery, 292 hp combined, improved electric range (G20 LCI)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 330e is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 330e Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 330e is powered by the B48 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine - the same engine used across BMW's modular family. While the B48 is significantly more reliable than its N20 predecessor, it has well-documented weaknesses including cooling system leaks, oil filter housing failures, and VANOS solenoid issues. The hybrid system adds complexity, with the 12V battery being a common source of drivetrain fault codes. Rebuilt units supplied through our network include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series 330e B48 Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B48 engine uses plastic components in the cooling system - water pump, thermostat housing and coolant lines - which become brittle with age and heat cycles. The oil filter housing is also prone to cracking, causing both coolant and oil leaks.

repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early; prevents overheating
When overheating has caused head gasket or block damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 330e is worth £18,000-£45,000 depending on generation, condition and mileage. For high-value modern examples, a rebuilt engine at £4,500-£6,500 is well within the vehicle's value. For older F30 examples, assess the car's overall condition carefully before committing.
problems.recommendation: Preventative cooling system maintenance is essential for any 330e owner. Replacing the water pump and thermostat proactively at 60,000-80,000 miles costs £500-£900 at a specialist - far less than the £4,500-£6,500 for a full engine replacement after an overheating event. Regular coolant level checks and using BMW-approved coolant can help extend component life.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B48B20O1 BMW 3 Series 330e engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS & Timing Chain Issues - Why the BMW 3 Series 330e Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The B48 engine can suffer from VANOS solenoid clogging (oil sludge and debris buildup) and timing chain tensioner wear. While the B48 does not have the catastrophic guide failure issues of the N20, timing chain and VANOS problems have been reported, particularly on early 2016-2018 examples.

repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective fix; restores power and idle quality

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner, VANOS hubs
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if rattle or fault codes present
When chain failure has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 330e ranges from £18,000 to £45,000. For vehicles under warranty or with strong retained value, a timing chain replacement or full engine rebuild is often justified. For older high-mileage examples, evaluate the car's overall condition before committing to major work.
problems.recommendation: For early B48-engined 330es (2016-2018), regular oil changes with BMW-approved oil and using premium fuel are essential to prevent VANOS solenoid clogging. If you hear rattle on cold start or experience drivetrain fault codes, have the timing chain and VANOS system inspected immediately. Replacement costs £1,800-£3,000 at a specialist - far less than a full engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B48B20M0 BMW 3 Series 330e engine prices

problems.h4: 12V Battery & Hybrid System Faults - Why the BMW 3 Series 330e Shows Drivetrain Warnings
problems.rootCause: The 330e lacks a conventional alternator - the 12V system is charged via the high-voltage battery. A weak 12V battery (measured at 11.7-12.2V at rest) can collapse during cranking, triggering drivetrain and HV faults. The 2016-2020 330e was also subject to a starter relay recall over fire risk from corrosion.

repairOptions.longevity: Check if your VIN is affected
When 12V battery replacement doesn't resolve faults

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 330e is worth £18,000-£45,000. 12V battery replacement is a relatively low-cost fix (£200-£350) and should be the first step when drivetrain warnings appear.
problems.recommendation: If your 330e displays drivetrain fault codes, start with the 12V battery - it's the most common cause of electrical gremlins in PHEV BMWs. Check your VIN against the starter relay recall (2016-2020 models) and have the recall work completed free of charge at a BMW dealer.
